# Star-delta starter -- TIA Portal starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The function block's body is yours.*

**The task.** Start the motor in star -- main and star contactors -- change over to delta when motor.speed reaches the speed on the panel's pot, and drop everything on Stop. The changeover timing is yours: there is no timer in the starter. Star and delta closed together is a short circuit, and contacts close in 30 ms but take 45 ms to stop conducting, so wait for motor.staraux to fall before you energise delta.

**Done when.** The motor runs up in star, changes over at the pot's speed with a modest current step, and runs on in delta, and motor.breaker never drops. Drop star and energise delta in the same scan and the breaker trips, and stays tripped until somebody closes it by hand at the starter. Then load the machine (the starter's Motor Load) and start again: the star run-up takes about twice as long, so a changeover timed in seconds comes half way up it and draws nearly the direct-on-line current. Only motor.speed knows when the motor is ready.

## Set it up

1. In a project with an S7-1500 CPU: *External source files -> Add new
   external file*, pick `star_delta_start.scl`, then right-click it -> *Generate
   blocks from source*. That creates `FF_IO` and `"StarDeltaStart"`. One
   exercise per CPU: this `FF_IO` replaces any other one.
2. Call `"StarDeltaStart"` from OB1 (drag it into `Main`; TIA creates the
   instance DB).
3. Check `FF_IO`'s properties: *Optimized block access* off (the source sets
   it), *Accessible from HMI/OPC UA* and *Writable from HMI/OPC UA* on for
   every member (TIA's default). Without *Writable* every sensor reads FALSE
   forever.
4. Compile, download, RUN.

## Run it

Open the scene in FactoryForge first (pick "Star-delta starter" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/star_delta_start.json)), then attach
the sidecar with whichever driver reaches your CPU:

```bash
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver opcua-client --mapping examples/tia/star-delta-start/opcua_mapping.json -o url opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver s7-snap7 -o host <cpu-ip> -o db <FF_IO's number> --mapping examples/tia/star-delta-start/snap7_mapping.json
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver plcsim-advanced -o instance <name> --mapping examples/tia/star-delta-start/plcsim_mapping.json
```

(From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar` in place of
`factoryforge-sidecar`, run from the repository root so the paths resolve.)
To have it marked, run `python tools/grade.py --scene star-delta-start` in place
of the 3D scene and add the `--port` it prints to the same command.

The OPC UA namespace index is usually 3, not always: run
`factoryforge-sidecar browse opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840` once and fix `ns=` in
the mapping if yours differs.

## FF_IO

In declaration order. `PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp);
`PLC reads` is an input (a sensor, a button, a measurement). The two
directions never share a byte, so the snap7 driver never rewrites a bit your
program owns. `FF_IO` is 20 bytes. *Brief* marks the signals the task
names.

| Tag | Direction | Member | Type | Offset | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `current_gauge.value` | PLC writes | `CurrentGaugeValue` | Real | DBD0 | needle position, scale 0..120 A | yes |
| `motor.delta` | PLC writes | `MotorDelta` | Bool | DBX4.0 | delta contactor coil -- NEVER with star: together they short the supply | yes |
| `motor.main` | PLC writes | `MotorMain` | Bool | DBX4.1 | main contactor coil: feeds the motor windings | yes |
| `motor.star` | PLC writes | `MotorStar` | Bool | DBX4.2 | star contactor coil: ties the winding ends together (a third of the torque) | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | `PanelGreen` | Bool | DBX4.3 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | `PanelRed` | Bool | DBX4.4 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | `TowerGreen` | Bool | DBX4.5 | tower lamp, green | yes |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | `TowerRed` | Bool | DBX4.6 | tower lamp, red | yes |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | `TowerYellow` | Bool | DBX4.7 | tower lamp, yellow | yes |
| `motor.current` | PLC reads | `MotorCurrent` | Real | DBD6 | line current, A (full load 20 A) | yes |
| `motor.speed` | PLC reads | `MotorSpeed` | Real | DBD10 | motor speed, % of synchronous | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | `PanelSetpoint` | Real | DBD14 | the operator's pot, 50..95 % (starts at 85) | yes |
| `motor.breaker` | PLC reads | `MotorBreaker` | Bool | DBX18.0 | motor breaker, normally closed: TRUE = closed; trips on a star-delta short and stays tripped | yes |
| `motor.deltaaux` | PLC reads | `MotorDeltaaux` | Bool | DBX18.1 | delta contacts conducting | yes |
| `motor.mainaux` | PLC reads | `MotorMainaux` | Bool | DBX18.2 | main contacts conducting | yes |
| `motor.overload` | PLC reads | `MotorOverload` | Bool | DBX18.3 | thermal overload, normally closed: TRUE = OK, FALSE = tripped | yes |
| `motor.staraux` | PLC reads | `MotorStaraux` | Bool | DBX18.4 | star contacts conducting -- still TRUE for 45 ms after its coil drops | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | `PanelEstop` | Bool | DBX18.5 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | `PanelReset` | Bool | DBX18.6 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | `PanelStart` | Bool | DBX18.7 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | `PanelStop` | Bool | DBX19.0 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |

`int` travels as a `DInt` and `float` as a `Real`: the OPC UA driver writes
Int32 and Float, and a member of any other type is refused as a type mismatch.
Hold anything the scene must see for well over a second on OPC UA: an
S7-1500 forces a 1000 ms publishing interval on subscriptions, which is why the
driver polls by default.
